slides.say: Eight piggy banks stand in a row. The first holds five coins and the last holds forty-seven. Each piggy bank holds at least four more coins than the one before it. What is the exact range for the fourth piggy bank?

They ask for the exact range. That means the smallest and the biggest number of coins the fourth piggy bank can hold. [short pause] We'll solve it in two different ways, by understanding which way to push, and then by testing values from the choices.
at: They ask for the exact range

slides.say: [short pause] Let's start with the smallest. For the fourth piggy bank to be as small as possible, every piggy bank before it gets the least it can. Each one holds at least four more than the one before. So we add exactly four each time. Five, then five plus four is nine, then thirteen, then seventeen.
Can it be less? No, because every step needs at least four more. So the fourth holds at least seventeen. Choice numbers two and four don't start at seventeen, so they're out.

Now let's find the biggest. We work backwards from the last piggy bank, which holds forty-seven. To keep the fourth as big as possible, the steps after it are as small as they can be, four each. From the eighth back to the fourth is four steps. Forty-seven, then forty-seven minus four is forty-three, then thirty-nine, thirty-five, and thirty-one.

So the fourth holds at most thirty-one. Choice number three goes up to thirty-five, so it's out. The last bank can still hold forty-seven in both cases. Any extra coins fit in a bigger step, since four is only the minimum increase. Seventeen to thirty-one, choice number one is our answer.

[pause] Now let's test values from the choices. The choices are ranges. The right range holds every value that can happen, and no value that can't. So we test a number that some choices hold and others don't.

Choice number four starts at thirteen. Can the fourth piggy bank hold thirteen? From five, three steps of at least four each bring it to at least five plus twelve, seventeen. So thirteen is impossible, and choice number four is out.
at: and choice number four is out

slides.say: Choice number three goes up to thirty-five. Can the fourth hold thirty-five? Then four more steps of at least four each bring the last one to at least thirty-five plus sixteen, fifty-one. But the last holds forty-seven. So thirty-five is impossible, and choice number three is out.
at: and choice number three is out

slides.say: Now let's test seventeen. Choice number two starts at twenty-one, so it leaves seventeen out. Can the fourth hold seventeen? Five, nine, thirteen, seventeen, then twenty-one, twenty-five, twenty-nine, and a big step to forty-seven. Every step is at least four. So seventeen happens, and choice number two is out. Choice number one is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: and choice number two is out
Choice number one is our answer
